content.value_statement: Unknown network protocols are hard to inspect, document, and debug. This skill guides packet capture, binary parsing, protocol signatures, and controlled validation workflows.
actual_capabilities: Guides traffic capture with Wireshark, tcpdump, tshark, mitmproxy, and Burp Suite.
Provides filters and workflows for TCP, HTTP, TLS, and custom protocol traffic.
Explains binary protocol structures, TLV parsing, length fields, and hex dump analysis.
Includes templates for protocol specifications and custom Wireshark dissectors.
Shows controlled fuzzing, packet replay, and validation using Scapy and Boofuzz.
limitations: Does not guarantee that traffic capture is legal or authorized.
Does not automatically analyze live networks or run tools by itself.
Requires packet captures, lab access, or user-provided protocol samples.
May need adaptation for encrypted, proprietary, or changing protocols.

use_cases.title: Document an Unknown Protocol
use_cases.description: Map message boundaries, fields, state transitions, and examples from captured traffic.

use_cases.title: Debug Network Communication
use_cases.description: Inspect packet flows, filters, protocol signatures, and TLS metadata during troubleshooting.

use_cases.title: Build a Parser or Dissector
use_cases.description: Turn observed structures into parser logic, documentation, and Wireshark dissector plans.

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a Capture
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner analysis of a packet capture.
prompt_templates.prompt: Help me inspect this packet capture. Identify likely protocols, useful Wireshark filters, and the first observations to record.

prompt_templates.title: Map Message Fields
prompt_templates.prompt: I have several binary messages from the same protocol. Help me infer headers, length fields, message types, and repeated patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Protocol Specification
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a protocol specification outline from these observations. Include transport, message format, state machine, examples, and open questions.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Controlled Validation
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an authorized lab validation plan for this protocol. Include parser checks, replay scope, fuzzing limits, safety controls, and evidence to collect.

output_examples.input: I have TCP traffic on an unknown port and several repeated binary messages.
output_examples.output: A staged analysis plan with capture checks, stream grouping, candidate header fields, length validation, and documentation tasks.

output_examples.input: I need to document a custom protocol for internal interoperability work.
output_examples.output: A protocol specification outline covering transport, message format, field tables, state transitions, examples, and unresolved assumptions.

output_examples.input: I want to test whether my parser handles malformed messages safely.
output_examples.output: A controlled validation checklist with lab scope, sample selection, fuzzing limits, crash triage, and cleanup steps.

best_practices: Work only on traffic and systems where you have explicit authorization.
Capture multiple sessions before inferring message fields or state transitions.
Store packet captures, TLS logs, and private keys with restricted access.
anti_patterns: Do not run MITM capture or replay against third-party systems without consent.
Do not treat one packet sample as a complete protocol specification.
Do not leave TLS key logs or packet captures in shared temporary directories.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps analyze network traffic, infer protocol structures, document formats, and plan controlled validation.

faq.question: Does it run packet capture tools automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and examples, but the user controls all tools and environments.

faq.question: Can it analyze encrypted traffic?
faq.answer: It can guide TLS metadata review and lawful decryption workflows when authorized key material is available.

faq.question: Is this suitable for production testing?
faq.answer: Use it first in labs or approved maintenance windows. Active replay and fuzzing can disrupt services.

faq.question: What inputs work best?
faq.answer: Packet captures, hex samples, observed message flows, protocol notes, and clear authorization boundaries work best.

faq.question: Which tools are referenced?
faq.answer: The playbook references Wireshark, tshark, tcpdump, mitmproxy, Burp Suite, Scapy, and Boofuzz.
